uncited: Topology and Ambiguity Handling addresses the topological inconsistencies that arise in standard Marching Cubes when processing ambiguous voxel configurations (cases 46, 47, 98, 99, 210, 213, 214, 215) [10327-lookup-table-and-ambiguity-handling].

These cases contain saddle points where the isosurface passes through the cube center, and the standard Lookup Table uses a fixed triangulation that can cause cracks or holes if adjacent voxels resolve the ambiguity differently [10327-lookup-table-and-ambiguity-handling].
This family provides methods to ensure manifold topology and consistent surface connectivity across voxel boundaries.
The family operates on the 256 binary configurations of a voxel's eight corner signs relative to an isovalue [10327-lookup-table-and-ambiguity-handling].
The core problem is that the standard `triangleTable` [10327-lookup-table-and-ambiguity-handling] does not guarantee topological consistency for the 8 ambiguous cases.
Standard implementations resolve these by selecting a single triangulation from the possible topologies, which may conflict with the resolution chosen by a neighbor sharing the saddle point.
The methods in this family either modify the dual structure to enforce manifold constraints or decompose the surface into disjoint patches to isolate topological ambiguities.
The issue of topological ambiguity in Marching Cubes was identified early in the method's history.

The standard 256-case lookup table, while efficient, does not account for the topological consistency required for a manifold mesh when saddle points are present [10327-lookup-table-and-ambiguity-handling].
Subsequent research has focused on resolving these ambiguities either by modifying the dual structure to enforce manifold constraints or by decomposing the surface into disjoint patches.
